thread.title: Tech Today: Apple’s Revenge, Snap Unstructured, Google’s Headaches

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Apple’s Revenge, Snap Unstructured, Google’s Headaches
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated May 2, 2018 10:29 a.m. ET Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Apple’s Revenge
Apple ( AAPL ) shares are up $6.99, or 4%, to $176.09, holding on to much of last night’s gains , after its fiscal Q2 results and outlook, and the expanded capital-returns plan , were better than much of the worst speculation heading into the report.
Think of it as Apple’s revenue on the naysayers.
Price targets are rising at some shops. More significant, perhaps, is that some are taking note of services revenue, which took over as the growth engine, in the words of Morgan Stanley ’s Katy Huberty , who has an Overweight rating on the shares, and a $200 price target.
The 31% growth in services was higher than the 27% growth Apple delivered in the December quarter, "despite significant scale” at $33 billion in trailing 12-months revenue.
"We don't see Services growth slowing anytime soon given the many growth levers,” she concludes, including the fact fewer than half of Apple's users pay for services, "and the paying customer base is growing strong double-digits."
Even the bears have to give it to them: Raymond James’s Chris Caso , who has a Market Perform rating on the shares, writes the company is “not going down without a fight."
But he’s just as skeptical as before, writing, "Looking forward, Apple didn’t provide enough information to fully vindicate iPhone X nor indicate its failure, so we don’t think investor concerns about iPhone units or mix will likely be put to rest until 4Q sell-through data is available in the fall."
Snap’s Lack of Structure
Snap ( SNAP ) was, of course, quite another story, as its quarterly revenue missed consensus estimates and the company warned things could get worse this quarter, as Jon Swartz wrote .
Snap is down $2.83, or 20%, to $11.30, compounding last night’s after-hours losses.
Piper Jaffray’s Sam Kemp , who has a Neutral rating on the shares and lowered the price target to $11.50 from $17, writes that "Snap is a poorly structured company that is demonstrating a clear pattern of mismanagement."
The company faces engineering challenges, notes Kemp, such as product reliability issues with its Android client app, but, "Despite these engineering challenges, Snap has rapidly shifted its priorities to profitability.” Its priorities seem strange to him — “for example, is now the time to be allocating resources to new Snapchat Spectacles?"
Facebook Rolls New Features
Shares of Facebook ( FB ) are up $2.91, or 1.7%, to $176.78 after Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg hosted the opening day of the company’s annual F8 developer conference, which Jon chronicled yesterday.
Although issues such as elections and fake news were to some extent addressed by Zuckerberg, the Street is mainly interested in a slew of new product features, including the dating service, which yesterday pressured shares of Match Group ( MTCH ), owners of Match.com and Tinder . Match today is bouncing back a little, up 10 cents at $36.81.
Other highlights include the ability to clear browsing history, and turn off storage of such information for the future; a new tab in Facebook for group discussions; and a new organization for Instagram ’s layout that can cluster things based on themes of subjects of interest.
Google’s Headaches
Interesting piece on the cover of today’s The Wall Street Journal by Kirsten Grind and Douglas MacMillan looking into the workspace strife at Alphabet ’s ( GOOGL ) Google , "where fractious groups of employees have turned the workplace into a virtual war zone of debate over all manner of social and political beliefs."
The article goes through the various ins and outs of employees with different agendas and points of view, and the company’s struggle to deal with a workplace culture that has encouraged free-wheeling debate.
The summation seems to come in the line: “They think they can please everybody, and I don’t think that’s possible,” said Tim Chevalier, the transgender former engineer.
Alphabet stock today is up 53 cents to $1,041.33.
